links_touching_record.rationale: FB2-SW-SIR-000001 is the software interface requirement set for the acquisition and monitoring boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000001 (AFE measurement driver API) and FB2-SW-IFS-000002 (SOA supervision). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.

The second specification FB2-SW-SIR-000001 is derived from. FB2-SW-SIR-000001 covers the acquisition and monitoring boundary and its derivation field names every interface specification it came from; this link names the second one so that a reader following the requirement to its evidence reaches both specifications rather than only the first. The direction and the reason are the same as for the first specification: the specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source, and the requirement states what must be true of it.

asil_justification.statement: Not applicable, and deliberately so. This requirement carries no safety allocation because the item it describes has not been through a hazard analysis and risk assessment, so there is no severity or exposure rating to derive an ASIL from. No ASIL is asserted for the real product and none is asserted here. This is not a statement that the interface is unimportant: it is a statement that the classification apparatus is not available in this repository, and a reader must not read 'not_applicable' as 'no consequence'.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent. It is a derivation from an analysed specification, not an elicitation, not an analysis of a higher-level requirement, and not independent review.

derivation.authoring_independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent from the interface specifications and the source. No requirements engineer confirmed that this is the interface that was wanted, no stakeholder stated a need that these requirements answer, and no human approved them. They record what the code obliges a consumer to rely on; they do not record what anyone asked for.
derivation.method: Every statement below names the interface element it obliges and the analysed behaviour it rests on. None of them introduces an obligation the source does not already impose.

element_requirements.basis: Each is declared to return STD_RETURN_TYPE_e, a two-value enum, and the interface specification records that STD_NOT_OK is the only negative value.
element_requirements.source_element: IFSE-000001 AFE_TriggerIc, IFSE-000003 AFE_StartMeasurement, IFSE-000004 AFE_RequestTemperatureRead
element_requirements.statement: A request to the acquisition interface shall report whether the request was accepted.

element_requirements.basis: The start request returns STD_RETURN_TYPE_e at acceptance only, and the completion query returns bool; the interface specification records that no completion notification is offered by the request itself.
element_requirements.statement: A consumer shall be able to determine separately whether the first measurement cycle has completed, because the request that starts it returns before the measurement exists.

element_requirements.basis: The forwarding wrapper asserts string < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS before the call, so the bound is enforced one level above the declared interface.
element_requirements.statement: Every string-addressed request parameter on the acquisition interface shall be bounded by the configured string count, and a value outside that bound shall be rejected before the request reaches the driver.

element_requirements.basis: All three are declared void and their bodies consist of DIAG_Handler calls; the interface specification records that a caller learns the outcome only by later reading diagnosis state.
element_requirements.source_element: IFSE-000101 SOA_CheckVoltages, IFSE-000102 SOA_CheckTemperatures, IFSE-000103 SOA_CheckCurrent
element_requirements.statement: The supervision interface shall deliver its entire effect through the diagnosis module and shall not rely on a return value to report a detected violation.

element_requirements.basis: Reached only through BMS_Trigger, which is called from the 10 ms cyclic task whose cycle time is 10 ms.
element_requirements.statement: The supervision interface shall be invoked on the 10 ms cycle.

record_verbatim.element_requirements_note: The failure reaction of this boundary is a precondition trap rather than a reported event. The analysed implementation enforces three of these five requirements with assertions and one with task placement, so a breach of the string bound, of the contactor-type bound or of the period stops the task or changes its latency instead of raising a diagnosis event. This is recorded rather than presented as a design choice, and it is the single most important thing a reader of this requirement set needs to know about it: none of these requirements has a detection channel of its own.
record_verbatim.failure_reaction: A violation of any of these is not observable as a returned error at the point of the requirement. C-E are enforced by assertions and by task placement rather than by a diagnostic, so their failure mode is a trap or a latency change, not an event.
not_established_by_this_record: The three existing software requirements in this corpus are back-inferred from the implementation and say nothing about interfaces. This record does not replace them and does not claim to supersede them; it adds the interface family that was absent and it names the direction it was produced in, which the existing records do not.

No requirement here is elicited from a stakeholder, a system requirement or a safety goal. Each states an obligation the existing code already imposes, which means none of them can be used to justify changing that code without a separate decision to do so.
No ASIL, no safety allocation, no conformity claim, no certification, no human approval. The asil field is not_applicable and the reason is recorded in asil_justification rather than left blank.
No verification has been performed against any of these requirements and no test measure exists for any of them. Every derivation in this record is an inspection of the source, not a test.

Nothing here is a hardware interface requirement. Where this boundary would need a physical contract - a sense range, an accuracy, a sampling time - no such requirement exists, because the hardware design that would carry it is external to this repository and FB2-HW-HDD-000001 records why.
record_verbatim.rationale: The requirements exist because the interface specifications analysed at the pinned commit show that this boundary has four properties a consumer must be able to rely on, and that none of them is stated by the interface itself. Without these requirements a consumer would have to read the implementation to learn them, which is what an interface requirement is supposed to prevent. The four properties are: a request result that distinguishes acceptance from rejection; a separate completion signal, because the request returns before the measurement exists; a bounded string argument, because the enforcement is an assertion in a wrapper rather than a returned error; and side-effect-only supervision, because the supervision entry points return nothing at all.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Four interface requirements over the acquisition and monitoring boundary, derived from FB2-SW-IFS-000001 and FB2-SW-IFS-000002. Each statement is one obligation a consumer of the boundary may rely on, and each is traceable to a specific analysed interface element rather than to a wish.

safety_allocation.mitigation: No ASIL is allocated to this requirement. It is a software interface requirement about how two modules call each other, and the product it describes has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment: no ISO 26262 conformity, no ASIL determination and no certification is claimed for it or for anything in this corpus. The non-applicability is stated with its reason rather than left blank, because an unexplained non-applicability is indistinguishable from a requirement that quietly dropped out of every ASIL-derived view.

record_verbatim.statement: The acquisition and monitoring interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a request entry point whose result reports acceptance or rejection; (b) a completion query by which a consumer can determine whether the first measurement cycle has completed; (c) a string-addressed request whose argument range is bounded by the configured string count; and (d) a supervision entry point that is invoked on the 10 ms cycle and whose entire effect is delivered through the diagnosis module rather than through a return value.
record_verbatim.title: Software interface requirements: the acquisition and monitoring interfaces

That is the accurate position, not a gap to be filled by writing more prose.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SW-SIR-000001` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record
6. a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role and whose description records the approval and cites the signed packet

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
